newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips sells 25 percent Bang & Olufsen stake.
newsitem.headline: Philips sells 25 percent Bang & Olufsen stake.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said Tuesday it had agreed to sell its 25 percent stake in Denmark's Bang & Olufsen A/S to Bang & Olufsen Holding for about 160 million guilders ($84 million).
Philips bought its stake in the chic Danish audio components and television maker in 1990 for about 100 million guilders ($52.5 million) as part of a deal to cement a cooperation pact.

"When we took the 25 percent shareholding in 1990, it was attached to an agreement to work closely together. Now seven years later the companies are satisfied with this cooperation," Philips spokesman Ben Geerts said.

"The contract will be extended for another five years and Philips maintains the status of preferred supplier. We feel and Bang & Olufsen feels that it's not necessary, per se, to maintain the participation because B&O's financial situation has improved," he added.
Philips and B&O said that a substantial economic recovery in recent years had enabled B&O to buy back the stake and become the sole shareholder in its audio and video subsidiary.

"We have substantial excess cash and it is in the interest of both the group and its shareholders to use part of that liquidity for this purpose, as long as this does not affect our successful cooperation with Philips," B&O Chairman Anders Knutsen said in a joint statement.

The Dutch company said that B&O had steadily increased its purchase of components from Philips since the agreement started in 1990 and added the cooperation had functioned satisfactorily for both parties.

Bang & Olufsen makes audio equipment for the exclusive luxury goods market, as well as making telephones and medical equipment. In January it reported half-year pre-tax and minorities profits of 174 million crowns ($27.6 million) and forecast a 20 percent rise in full-year results.
Analysts welcomed the deal as fitting in with Philips' strategy of streamlining its organisation and wringing cash flow from the business, as well as promoting the Philips brand.
